config._note: Hub archetype: Employee is the record every other HR/payroll schema in humaniq points AT (EmploymentContract.employeeId, Payslip.employeeId, Timesheet.employeeId, Expense.employeeId — all now canonical $ref relations, ADR-062 rule 7), so the page's job is to be the single place an HR/payroll admin lands to see one person's whole labour and pay picture. ADR-062 round-2 rework: the data widget is SPLIT into 'Person' (employeeNumber/firstName/lastName/dateOfBirth/bsn — the identity attributes) at 8-wide beside an in-grid stats-block (KPIs, top-right — replaces the deprecated summaryAggregates header chips) at 4-wide; 'Employment & compliance' (startDate/endDate/grossMonthlySalary/taxTableColor/ID-document retention/30%-ruling incl. start/end date + reduced-norm flag (30-procent-regeling)/A1 posting/jurisdiction-specific onboarding flags — 21 fields, genuinely this schema's bulk) runs full-width below since it has no natural width-4 partner. Contracts and Timesheets are paired FK-scoped lists, then Payslips (allowCreate:false — payroll-generated, not hand-created from here) and Expenses, then org-chart-basic (2026-07-13) adds an Assignments FK-scoped list (OrgAssignment.employeeId — the placements this employee holds across the org hierarchy) as a full-width row, and performance-reviews-mvp (2026-07-13) adds a Beoordelingen FK-scoped list (PerformanceReview.employeeId — the ADR-001 Rule 6 dossier anchoring: performance data lives on the personnel dossier, not a separate module) as a further full-width row, and goals-okr (2026-07-15) adds a Doelen & OKR's FK-scoped list (Objective.employeeId — the measurable, cross-review sibling of Beoordelingen; team objectives live on OrgUnit and do not appear here) as a further full-width row, and comp-cycles (2026-07-15) adds a Beloningsvoorstellen FK-scoped list (CompAdjustment.employeeId — the ADR-001 Rule 6 'Functie & comp' detail-surface anchoring: compensation-review proposals live on the personnel dossier, not a separate module) as a further full-width row, and leave-buy-sell (2026-07-15) adds a Verlof kopen/verkopen FK-scoped list (LeaveTransaction.employeeId, rowRoute LeaveTransactionDetail) as a further full-width row, before the personnel-file Files leaf, which shifts down again. Files is justified by identityDocumentVerified/identityDocumentRetainedUntil/loonheffingenVerklaringOnFile — real statutory document-retention fields on this schema, not a generic add. NO calendar/contacts/talk: Employee declares no appointment or comms linkedType — the person's own identity data lives on this record, it is not a link to a separate NC contact. No lifecycleActions — Employee carries no x-openregister-lifecycle. Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

widgets.title: Contracts
widgets._note: `entries` is a FLAT prop. CnStatsBlockWidget declares dataSource/entries/title/countLabel/variant/showZeroCount/horizontal/route/iconClass and no `content` prop at all, so the previous `content: {entries: […]}` shape never reached the component — it errored `Exactly one of dataSource / entries must be provided`. That error was invisible until the dashboard widget catalog started resolving at all (see src/main.js): with the catalog empty, CnWidgetGrid never mounted the component and never ran its contract check.

config._note: Financial-document archetype (x-schema-org: schema:Invoice), same family as Expense's amount-first design: three headline tiles (gross pay, net pay, Related-to-Employee) lead the page since that is what an employee or approver checks first, followed by the dense data widget carrying the full gross-to-net withholding breakdown (NL loonheffing/zvw/wkr, DE Lohnsteuer/Soli/Kirchensteuer, FR cotisations/PAS, US FICA/Medicare -- the schema is genuinely multi-jurisdiction: only one jurisdiction's fields populate per real record, but which one varies per payslip so a static manifest cannot cherry-pick per-instance; all fields surface via one widget, sized to its true field count and set to 4 columns full-width rather than clipped at 2). ADR-062 round-2: data widget now excludes employeeId (resolved via Related instead of raw uuid) and the height budget was corrected from the round-1 h7 (which clipped ~54 fields behind a scrollbar) to match content. Stat format uses 'number' not 'currency' because Payslip.currency varies per record (EUR/USD) and a widget's format is static. No files/calendar/comms leaves: nothing in the schema models an attachable payslip document or appointment, and Payslip carries no x-openregister-lifecycle so there are no lifecycleActions. Audit history is a sidebar tab. payslip-pdf-docudesk (2026-07-14): page-level action "Genereer PDF" mirrors EmploymentContractDetail's "Genereer arbeidsovereenkomst" shape -- POST /api/documents/generate with {payslipId: @objectId, documentType: loonstrook}, guarded server-side by DocumentController::authorizePayslip().

config._note: Batch/reconciliation archetype: a PayrollRun is a per-period aggregate of an administration's payslips, so its page leads with the GL-reconciliation totals (totalGross/totalNet/withholdingLiabilityBalance -- exactly the numbers xc-payroll-gl-reconciliation and xc-withholding-liability-clearing check) as stat KPIs, then the full record (period/administrationId/jurisdiction/status/glLiabilityPosted/glExpensePosted/withholdingsClearedToZero plus the engine stamps engineVersion/calculatedAt) in the data widget below. payroll-core-engine (2026-07-14): Payslip NOW carries a real payrollRunId $ref back to PayrollRun (added by payroll-core-schema), so the page gains the FK-scoped Payslips child list (allowCreate:false -- generation via the engine is the only create path, design.md D5) and the page-level api-call action "(Her)berekenen" (POST /api/payroll/calculate with {runId: @objectId}, guarded server-side by PayrollController::authorizeRun(), draft-only -- non-draft runs get a 400). Still NO lifecycleActions: `status` is a plain enum (draft/approved/posted/paid) with no `x-openregister-lifecycle` transition map on this schema -- driving lifecycleActions here would invent transition names the backend does not guard; the recalculate action is a page action, not a transition. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._note: Statutory-deadline archetype: a filing's whole purpose is 'was it filed on time and is proof retained'. loonaangifte-filing-lifecycle (2026-07-12) gave NL filings a real create->review->confirm->send workflow, so the page now leads with a compact status/tijdvakcode/deadline/response widget (fi-status) before the full filing data widget, and exposes the klaarzetten/bevestigen/verzenden/heropenen/corrigeren transitions via lifecycleActions (Timesheet pattern). No stats-block KPI tile is used for Status/Deadline: the vendored app-manifest-v2 schema's stat/stats-block `metric` only supports count/sum aggregation, which cannot echo a non-numeric field (enum/date) of the current object, so fi-status is a `data` widget instead -- schema-valid and functionally equivalent (prominent, top-of-page). No related panel (the schema carries no employeeId/administrationId or any other object-FK -- a filing is an organisation-level record, not scoped to a person). Files is included full-width for the filed submission/deposit proof, justified by the schema's own retainedUntil/furnishedToRecipientDate/filedWithAuthorityDate retention-evidence fields (NL 7yr / DE 6yr / US 4yr retention obligations). No calendar/comms leaves -- deadline is a plain date field, not an appointment/event linkedType. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

payroll-mutation-reports (2026-07-14): a PayrollMutationReport is a PURE, read-only diff snapshot -- never recomputed, never written outside PayrollMutationService (design.md D3) -- so the page leads with the accountant's headline (totalWageCostDelta) plus the entered/left/changed counts as stat KPIs (the PayrollRunDetail stat-tile precedent), then the full record (header fromRunId/toRunId/fromPeriod/toPeriod/administrationId/generatedAt, the four component deltas, the four counts, and the embedded per-employee `lines` array) in the pmr-data widget below -- the PayrollGLPostDetail precedent for an embedded array snapshot rendered inside a plain data widget (its own `lines` field, same shape: a system-generated audit-style record, not user-editable). No lifecycleActions: the schema carries no x-openregister-lifecycle -- a report is either regenerated (superseding this one in place, design.md D7) or not; there is no user-facing status transition to guard. No Files/calendar/comms leaves -- not a document or event. Admin/HR only, mirroring the Payroll nav group.

wkr-administration (2026-07-15): a WkrAssessment is the persisted computed summary AND reporting record (design.md D1) -- the PayrollMutationReportDetail stat-tile precedent: four headline KPIs (fiscale loonsom, vrije ruimte, vrije-ruimte used, eindheffing due) lead the page since that is the exposure question an accountant checks first, then the full record (status/engineVersion/assessedAt/excess/eindheffingRate) in the wa-data widget below. No lifecycleActions: the schema carries no x-openregister-lifecycle -- an assessment is either (re)computed (upserting in place, design.md D5) or not; there is no user-facing status transition to guard, only the Beoordelen recompute action (backed by PayrollController::wkrAssess(), the mutations()/adjust() no-admin-idor + admin/HR-gate precedent). No Files/calendar/comms leaves -- not a document or event. Admin/HR only, mirroring the Payroll nav group. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

params.title: Contract
params.note: Leaf compliance record: no other schema in humaniq references EmploymentContract by FK, so the page is a simple two-panel layout -- the data widget (type/writtenContract/dates/hoursPerWeek/hourlyWage/cao/caoSchaal/awfTariff plus the jurisdiction-specific fields: workingTimeDocumented, overtimeMultiplier, ftePartOfYearMinijob, dpaeFiledBeforeStart) at 8-wide, excluding employeeId since the Related panel already resolves and links the owning Employee by name -- and Related at 4-wide for that one meaningful outbound ref. cao-library (2026-07-14): the ct-data widget excludes only employeeId, so the contract's cao (the referenced CAO library id) and caoSchaal (its pay scale) render here for free -- no widget change needed. No child lists (nothing points at a contract), no files/calendar/comms leaves (no linkedType or document field evidence on this schema), no lifecycleActions (EmploymentContract has no x-openregister-lifecycle). Audit history is a sidebar tab. functiehuis-hr21 (2026-07-18): the ct-data widget now also excludes normfunctieId (the new $ref, the employeeId precedent) -- the Related panel resolves and links the assigned Normfunctie by name for free, confirmed rendering the contract's HR21 function assignment.
